source_text:
Αὕτη δὲ καὶ μόνη θεία φύσει
πρόοδος, εἴπερ δεῖ φύσει λέγειν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑπερφυῶν καὶ θείων· καὶ ταύτης ἀρχὴ μὲν
ἄναρχος ὁ Πατὴρ, ἐξ αὐτοῦ γάρ· μεσότης δὲ σύναρχος ὁ Υἱὸς, δι' αὐτοῦ γάρ· τέλος δὲ
ὑπερτελέστατον καὶ ἀτελεύτητον τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, εἰς αὐτὸ γάρ· ἐξῄρηται δὲ καὶ
τῶν ἄλλων προόδων αὕτη· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐξίστησιν ὅλως τῆς ἀρχῆς τὰ ἐξ αὐτῆς, ἀλλ'
ἀνεκ- φοίτητα πάντη ταύτης τηρεῖ, διὰ τὴν τῆς οὐσίας ταυτότητα· εἰ καὶ ὡς ἴδια
πρόσωπα πρόεισι· διὸ οὐδὲ τῆς κατ' ἔφεσιν ἐπιστροφῆς δέονται· αἱ δὲ παρὰ ταύτην
πᾶσαι τῶν ὄντων πρόοδοι, τοῖς οὖσι συνδιαιροῦνται· καὶ ἄναρχος μὲν τούτων
οὐδεμία, ὅτι καὶ τῶν ὄντων ἄναρχον οὐδὲν, ἀλλὰ πάντα γέγονε παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς διὰ
τοῦ Υἱοῦ συντελεσθέντα τῷ Πνεύματι· ἀτελεύτητος δὲ, οὐ πᾶσα· οὔτε μὴν πάντη,
ἀλλὰ τῶν μὲν ἀϊδίων μετὰ τὴν ἐκεῖθεν παραγωγὴν μενόντων, ἡ μὲν κατ' οὐσίαν καὶ
δὴ τετέλεσται· οὔτε γὰρ ἀλλάττα παρὰ τὰ ἐξ ἀρχῆς παραχθέντα ἐπιπαράγονται· οὔτ'
thought_title: The one divine procession alone is unoriginate and endless
orientation: Procopius continues his refutation of Proclus, now distinguishing the unique divine procession of the Trinity from all processions of created things.
pass_a_gloss: And this is the only procession by nature divine, if indeed one must say 'by nature' in the case of things beyond nature and divine. And of this procession the beginning is the unoriginate Father, for it is from him. And the middle is the Son, co-unoriginate with the Father, for it is through him. And the end is the utterly perfect and endless Holy Spirit, for it is into him. And this procession is set apart also from the other processions. For it does not at all make the things that come from it stand outside the beginning, but it keeps them wholly not departing from it, because of the sameness of the essence, even if they proceed as distinct persons. Therefore they do not need the return according to desire. But all the processions of beings besides this one are distinguished along with the beings. And none of these is without a beginning, because also none of the beings is without a beginning, but all things have come into being from the Father through the Son, completed in the Spirit. And not every one is endless, nor indeed wholly so. But of the eternal things, after their production from there, remaining, the procession according to essence has indeed been completed. For neither are other things besides the things produced from the beginning produced in addition. Nor

choices.why: Literal rendering of the dative of respect, preserving the philosophical force of the qualification.
Literal compound rendering to keep the 'hyper-' prefix visible, matching the author's contrast with 'by nature'.
Keeps the spatial metaphor of beginning-middle-end that structures the sentence.
Preserves the superlative and the 'hyper-' prefix, which is theologically loaded here.
Renders the alpha-privative compound literally to show the negation of departure from the source.
Literal rendering of the prepositional phrase, preserving the technical sense of the return by desire.

pass_b_english: This, then, is the only procession that is divine by nature, if indeed one should speak of nature at all in the case of things beyond nature and divine. Its beginning is the unoriginate Father, for it is from Him. Its middle is the Son, who shares that unoriginate beginning, for it is through Him. Its end, most super-perfect and endless, is the Holy Spirit, for it is in Him.

This procession is also set apart from the others. It does not make the things that come from it stand outside the origin at all. Rather, it keeps them from ever departing from that origin, because of the sameness of essence, even though they proceed as distinct persons. For this reason they have no need of the return according to desire.

But all the processions of beings besides this one are divided together with the beings themselves. None of these processions is unoriginate, because no being is unoriginate. Rather, all things have come into being from the Father through the Son and have been completed in the Spirit. Not every one of these processions is endless, nor is any of them endless in every respect.

For the eternal things remain after their production from there, and their procession according to essence has indeed been completed. No other things are produced in addition to those that were produced from the beginning.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'pair' for δυάς concept, but σύναρχος here means 'co-unoriginate'/'sharing the unoriginate nature', not 'shares that origin'.
ἀνεκφοίτητα means 'not going out/away from', i.e., not departing; 'un-departed' is awkward and unclear—suggests something not left behind rather than not departing.

problems.quote: its middle is the Son, who shares that origin
problems.why: σύναρχος means 'co-unoriginate', i.e., sharing the unoriginate nature with the Father, not merely 'shares that origin' which could mean derivative sharing; this is a major theological claim about the Son's eternal generation.
problems.fix: its middle is the Son, co-unoriginate with Him
problems.ruling: σύναρχος = co-unoriginate; 'shares that origin' risks implying derivative sharing, losing the key theological claim of co-eternal unoriginate status.
